clue.text: Investment finally successful with a horse

definitions.text: Investment finally successful with a horse

parts.words: Investment finally successful with a horse
parts.note: investment is the military sense, a siege; the siege of Troy ended only when the Greeks smuggled soldiers in inside a wooden horse

explanation.surface: A financier's punt finally pays off thanks to a racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' looks financial and 'horse' looks like the turf, but investment here means besieging a city, and the horse is the wooden one left at the gates of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: The decade-long Greek siege of Troy was ended by the ruse of the wooden horse, as told in Homer and Virgil.

clue.text: Region's followed broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the word for followed is heard rather than seen

parts.note: to have followed someone is to have tracked them

explanation.surface: A region has been tracked by the broadcaster's cameras.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a stretch or expanse of land, a synonym for a region or area.

clue.text: Water-plant we rowed around

indicators.note: around tells us one word goes round the other, here the word for rowed enclosing we

parts.note: to have oared a boat is to have rowed it

explanation.surface: Two rowers paddle around a plant growing in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Oarweed is a large brown seaweed, kelp, so a plant that lives in water.

clue.text: One better shot on land than at sea

definitions.text: One better shot on land than at sea

parts.words: One better shot on land than at sea
parts.note: in golf a score of three under par on a hole is prized, while sailors think the great seabird brings bad luck if shot, as in Coleridge's Ancient Mariner

explanation.surface: Something that is a better target ashore than out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: On land 'shot' is a golf stroke and the bird name is a score three under par; at sea, shooting the bird brought a curse on Coleridge's mariner.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a golf score three under par and the great seabird that sailors consider unlucky to kill.

clue.text: The very toy for a little squirt?

definitions.text: The very toy for a little squirt?

parts.words: The very toy for a little squirt?
parts.note: a little squirt is a small child, but also a small jet of liquid, which a plaything gun fires

explanation.surface: Just the plaything for a cheeky small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little squirt' is slang for a small annoying child, but the toy literally fires a little squirt of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's toy gun that fires a jet of liquid from a trigger-operated reservoir.

clue.text: Free travel curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means its tail is cut off, so the last letter of the word for travel goes

parts.note: to ride is to travel on horseback or in a vehicle

explanation.surface: Free travel has been cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' removes the last letter, E, from RIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rid a place of something is to free it of that thing, a straight synonym as a verb.

clue.text: Available on the way out

definitions.meaning: as in the best deal to be had, the one currently on offer
departing, leaving, or nearing an end

explanation.surface: Something on sale just as it is leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Going means obtainable (the going rate) and also departing, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Smile, eating a little salty bit

indicators.note: eating means the word for smile takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: Someone grinning while nibbling a salty snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A grain of salt is a single tiny particle of it.

clue.text: Hints the whole House is not truthful?

annotationWithheld.why: Hints the whole House is not truthful? (7): IMPLIES reads as MP + LIES for 'the whole House is not truthful', but no clue word supplies the I and no source found gives a parse or a fuller clue
annotationWithheld.clue: Hints the whole House is not truthful?

clue.text: Biscuit and egg in turn digested

indicators.note: digested food is broken down, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A biscuit and an egg eaten one after the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digested' shuffles EGG IN TURN into the biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gingernut is a hard, crunchy ginger-flavoured biscuit, a British teatime favourite.

clue.text: Athletic type driving killer back with club

indicators.note: driving back suggests pushing the word for killer backwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: the orca is the killer whale
a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: A sportsman drives off a murderer with a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving' belongs to the surface picture of beating off an attacker; 'back' alone signals the reversal, and the orca is the killer whale.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat is a gymnastic performer, certainly an athletic sort of person.

clue.text: Complete movement of camera without a flicker

parts.note: dead means complete or absolute, as in dead loss or dead centre
a pan is a sideways sweep of a camera

explanation.surface: A film director orders a full sweep of the camera with no wobble.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadpan describes an expressionless face or manner, showing not a flicker of emotion.

clue.text: Deal with letters regularly in three parts

indicators.note: taking letters regularly means picking every other one from the following words

explanation.surface: Handling correspondence spread evenly over three sections.
explanation.walkthrough: The first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of 'three parts' are picked.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a matter or a patient is to deal with it.

clue.text: Not forgetful of plunder outside shelter

indicators.note: outside means the word for plunder goes round the word for shelter

parts.note: to reive is an old Scots and Border word for raid or plunder
a tent is a canvas shelter

explanation.surface: Someone who remembers where the loot outside the tent was hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: REIVE is the verb behind the Border reivers, the raiders of the Anglo-Scottish frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A retentive memory holds on to things, so it is the opposite of forgetful.

clue.text: Eating 6 dn and rodent kills dinosaur

indicators.note: eating means the word for kills takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to top someone is slang for killing them
the clue points to the answer at 6 down, a grain, and rice is a grain
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A dinosaur that slays as it munches cereal and rats.
explanation.walkthrough: '6 dn' points at 6 down, GRAIN, here a pointer to rice, a grain, rather than to the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Triceratops was a large three-horned plant-eating dinosaur of the Cretaceous.

clue.text: Odd rhyme for cocoon

parts.note: read whimsically: a three-letter word that rhymes with odd and means a protective casing like a seed case

explanation.surface: A strange piece of verse about a cocoon.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue asks for a word that rhymes with 'odd' and also means a casing; only one short word does both.
explanation.definitionFit: A pod is a seed case or protective casing, much as a cocoon encases a pupa.

clue.text: Dickens hero made out to be harbouring extremely reasonable but vain hope TOLEI

parts.note: Pip is the hero of Dickens's Great Expectations

indicators.note: harbouring means holding something inside, so the shuffled word encloses the next piece
out means the letters of the next word are put out of order
extremely points to the extreme letters, the first and last of the following word

explanation.surface: A Dickens character is shown to be holding on to a sensible but futile wish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MADE to EDAM before 'to be harbouring' wraps it round the first and last letters of 'reasonable', picked by 'extremely'. The trailing 'TOLEI' is stray print from the page, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe dream is a fanciful, unattainable hope, originally the visions of an opium smoker.

clue.text: Reproduction's out? It ruins us all

definitions.meaning: if copies are out of fashion, then the genuine article is in fashion, read as a phrase
Christian doctrine of the sin inherited from Adam that corrupts every person

explanation.surface: A fashion verdict that copies are passé, and a warning that something brings everybody down.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is whimsical: if reproductions are out, the genuine article must be in.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian theology the inherited state of sin from Adam's fall taints all humanity.

clue.text: One refusing hard stuff cooked brains Check tod and ate

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or fiddled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teetotaller who cooked brains and ate them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges BRAINS with ATE; the words 'Check tod' are stray print from the page.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstainer refuses alcohol, which is the hard stuff, a common phrase for spirits.

clue.text: Leaders showing due deference to our compilers

parts.note: pace, from Latin, means with due respect to someone, used before disagreeing with them
setters are the people who compile crosswords

explanation.surface: Leaders who show proper respect to the people who make our puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: PACE is the Latin courtesy word used before contradicting someone, as in 'pace the experts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pace-setters lead the way and set the speed or standard that others follow.

clue.text: Stopping being excellent

definitions.meaning: putting a stopper in a bottle
dated British slang for splendid or first-rate

explanation.surface: Halting something in fine style.
explanation.definitionFit: Corking is plugging a bottle, and also old British slang meaning splendid.

clue.text: Egg, one not for everyone

indicators.note: not means the following piece is left out of the word for one

parts.note: a unit is a single thing, one
U is the British film certificate meaning universal, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: An egg that not everybody wants.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film classification for a film anyone may see.
explanation.definitionFit: A nit is the egg of a louse, as found in children's hair.

clue.text: Spaniard from the South showing love for English city

indicators.note: love for English means the letter for love takes the place of the letter for English
in a down clue, coming from the south means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: an Iberian is a native of the Iberian peninsula, so a Spaniard
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A Spanish lover in an English city, seen from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the South' reverses IBERIAN to NAIREBI; then O replaces E.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: All bored to distraction by a girl of Mozart's

indicators.note: driven to distraction suggests turmoil, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Everyone is driven mad with boredom by one of the composer's heroines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to distraction' rearranges ALL BORED into DORABELL, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorabella is one of the two sisters in Mozart's opera Cosi fan tutte.

clue.text: Made room in cottage: I'll shortly move in

indicators.note: move in means the next piece goes inside the word for the cottage room

parts.note: in Scots a but is the outer room of a two-roomed cottage, the but and ben

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: Space was made in the cottage because the speaker will soon move in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims the last letter of I'LL and 'move in' puts the result inside the cottage room; a 'but and ben' is a Scottish two-room cottage, the but being the outer room.
explanation.definitionFit: Built is the past tense of build, meaning constructed or made.

clue.text: Part of mansion perhaps making an impression

definitions.meaning: a side section of a large house, like the east one

explanation.surface: A grand house's extension that impresses visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing is a section of a large building, and awing means inspiring awe.

clue.text: Sawn-off weapon found on convict in camp

indicators.note: sawn-off means the end is cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
a lag is a convict, an old lag

explanation.surface: A sawn-off shotgun is found on a prisoner in a camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sawn-off' removes the last letter of the weapon, as a sawn-off shotgun loses the end of its barrel; 'found on' puts the convict after it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A gulag is a Soviet forced-labour camp.

clue.text: Exclusive type of Italian within European border

indicators.note: within means the next piece is placed inside the word for border

parts.note: a list is a border or edging strip, as on cloth
It is the abbreviation for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: A snobbish Italian living inside the borders of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: LIST in the sense of a selvage or edge strip is old but fair.
explanation.definitionFit: An elitist favours an exclusive select group and looks down on others.

clue.text: Fox, shut up, died

parts.note: a door pulled to is shut, so to means closed
d is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A fox is silenced and dies.
explanation.walkthrough: TOD is a Scots and northern English word for a fox.
explanation.definitionFit: A tod is a dialect name for a fox.

clue.text: Admit objective was a bad mistake

parts.note: to own up is to admit
a goal is an objective

explanation.surface: Confessing that the aim was a serious error.
explanation.walkthrough: In football an own goal is one scored against one's own side, hence a self-inflicted blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: An own goal is a self-defeating error, from football, where it puts the ball in your own net.

clue.text: Power of juvenile hearing

indicators.note: hearing tells us the word for juvenile is heard, not read

parts.note: a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: The strength of a young person's ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is strength or power, as in might is right.

clue.text: Expecting to receive heartless discipline in the army

indicators.note: heartless means the inside is removed, leaving only the outer letters of the next word

parts.note: serving soldiers are in the army

explanation.surface: Awaiting the heartless discipline of military life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves DE, the first and last letters of 'discipline'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deserving of something means being worthy and so in line to receive it.
